cards.text: John, son of Zechariah, has been preaching a baptism of repentance (Luke 3:2-3), and crowds of people are getting baptized. Jesus, Mary's son from Nazareth (Luke 1:31; 2:39), is baptized right along with them. No VIP line, no cutting ahead, just one more person in the water.

cards.question: Jesus has just been baptized. Heaven opens while He is teaching the crowd.
Heaven opens over Jesus while He prays. Who comes down on Him?

cards.text: The Holy Spirit comes down on Jesus in a bodily form, not a hunch, not a vibe. A SHAPE, friend, and I'm a cookie stamper, so shapes are my WHOLE career.

cards.question: The Holy Spirit comes down on Jesus in a bodily form like a ___.

cards.text: A DOVE. Friend, that's my Minty's shape, and when I read this part I got chills all the way down to my gold base.
Then a voice comes from heaven, talking right to Jesus.

cards.question: The voice from heaven speaks to Jesus. What does it call Him?
The voice from heaven also tells Jesus it is well pleased with Him.

cards.text: Then comes a detail about when Jesus begins His ministry. Friend, I sat in a drawer for YEARS before my big job showed up, so you KNOW I'm leaning in on this one.

cards.question: Jesus is about ___ years old when He begins His ministry.

cards.text: Then Luke, the writer of this Gospel, gives Jesus' family line, and friend, it's LONGER than every receipt in my old junk drawer stacked together. It starts with Joseph, since Jesus was regarded as his son, and runs back through David, Judah, Abraham and Noah, all the way to Adam, the son of God.

findings.problem: Cards 2, 3, 5, 8 and 11 all ask for details that the earlier cards neither supply nor make inferable: praying rather than teaching, the Holy Spirit, the dove, "My beloved Son" and Jesus' age. Nearly every choice is therefore discovery or luck rather than an informed guess.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The blank asks for "dove," the exact next word of a verse the baker has not yet seen. Card 4 establishes only that there was a bodily form, so the baker cannot reason out which word belongs in the blank.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: "A DOVE" drops the simile in Luke 3:22, which says the Holy Spirit descended "in a bodily form like a dove." As a standalone story card, this can turn the comparison into a statement that He was simply a dove.
This card only reacts to the previous answer and connects the dove with Minty. It adds no new moment or detail from the passage, so it functions as a recap rather than moving the walkthrough forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the unseen word "thirty." Card 10 gives no information from which Jesus' age can be reasoned, making this a wording guess rather than a meaning-based blank.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
